title: High-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries enabled by tailored sulfur–sulfide and sulfur–carbon interfaces - Nature Materials
byline: Cho; Yukio; Hongchang; Kim; Miso; King; Madison; Zhang; Zisheng; Patil; Shripad; Hwong; Jason; Liu; Haoyu; Duhan; Quan; Yifan; Zheng; Xueli; Tzeng; Yan-Kai; Sho
html:
Abstract

High energy density promised by solid-state batteries requires overcoming fundamental limitations in carrier transport. Although tortuous carrier pathways in high-loading cathodes are often viewed as the dominant bottleneck, we show that interfacial ion and electron transport is an even more critical lever for enhancing energy density in sulfide-based all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries. By enabling partial lithiation at the sulfur–sulfide interface and eliminating the electron-impeding oxidation layer at the sulfur–carbon interface, we achieve high-loading all-solid-state lithium–sulfur battery cathodes with areal capacities near 15 mAh cm−2 and sulfur utilization above 90% with a moderate stack pressure of 15–25 MPa. These metrics correspond to projected pouch-cell-level energy densities surpassing 500 Wh kg−1. Fast cycling at 1C retains 82.1% capacity over 500 cycles with Coulombic efficiencies up to 99.9%, and stable cycling is also achieved with a lithium metal anode at 10 MPa instead of the more common Li–In alloy. This work highlights the power of interfacial control within composite cathodes, and demonstrates another approach for designing high-energy-density all-solid-state lithium–sulfur batteries for next-generation energy storage.
